newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan's CPC defers 2H '97 diesel export tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's CPC defers 2H '97 diesel export tender.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has decided to defer floating its term tender to export diesel for second half 1997 liftings until after August due to current low regional prices, a CPC source said on Friday.
In turn, CPC decided to issue a second tender to sell its third spot cargo of 0.3 percent sulphur diesel for lifting in July.
The 225,000-to-250,000-barrel spot cargo is for July 23-27 lifting on a free-on-board (fob) Kaohsiung basis.
The spot tender closes on June 26 and offers will be valid for two days.
The term sales tender was scheduled to be issued this week for four to six cargoes to be lifted between July and December.
"We have decided to defer the term tender until after August," the CPC source told Reuters. "The actual date to issue the tender will depend on the market situation."
Diesel prices started plunging early last week and hit a 20-month low of $21.45 per barrel on Wednesday. It was hovering around $25.00 in early June.
But some traders believe that the market has hit its near term floor with bargain hunters emerging to take advantage of current low prices, and has started to rebound slightly since Thursday.
Swaps diesel values for July was indicated at $22.10/$22.20 per barrel, up from Thursday's $21.95/$22.05 and Wednesday's $21.50/$21.70.
Taiwan awarded two diesel contracts in its tender for January-June 1997 liftings to Singapore trader Hin Leong Trading at around 46 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, fob Kaohsiung.

CPC also awarded two contracts in its first diesel term sales tender for July-December 1996 liftings at around 40-50 cents above Singapore spot quotes, fob Kaohsiung, to Hin Leong Trading and BB Energy.
In its last spot tender, CPC sold two 225,000-to-250,000-barrel cargoes of 0.3-percent sulphur diesel for July 2-19 deliveries at $22.50-$23.00 per barrel, fob Kaohsiung basis.
Before that, CPC also sold two cargoes in its tender for June 4-17 liftings at around $24.60 per barrel, fob Kaohsiung.
